content:
I took Gogier: Oathbound all the way to Psyche Surge +12 and his Wheel of Destiny to +12.
I spent a significant amount of money on him because he is a brand-new limited Warden released in the Madness era. I wasn't expecting him to powercreep the entire game. I expected him to at least function properly in the endgame environment he was released into.
After actually playing him at max investment, I genuinely have no idea what happened during his design and testing.
thread_title: +12/+12 Gogier: Oathbound Is Still Awful in Madness. How Many Male Awakeners Have to Fail?

content:
1. He barely does his actual job as a Warden
Gogier is supposed to be a Warden.
So why are his defensive numbers this bad?
Even after fully stacking his passive, his Exalt barely gives a little over 1,000 Shield.
Meanwhile, in D-Effect Zone: Wave 5: Madness, there is an encounter where enemies can deal roughly 6,000 damage in a single turn.
How is that remotely proportional?
How is a little over 1,000 Shield supposed to deal with the damage pressure of the content he was literally released into?
His X-cost card has the exact same problem.
The STR reduction is too low.
The STR gain is too low.
The overall value is nowhere near good enough for the amount of Arithmetica you are expected to spend on it.
And then his passive wants you to fully spend an X-cost card five times to finish stacking his damage bonus.
So the intended gameplay is apparently:
Survive Madness-level incoming damage while repeatedly dumping 5 Arithmetica into an under-tuned X-cost card.
Alright.
You do it.
Show me how this character is supposed to stay alive while doing that.
thread_title: +12/+12 Gogier: Oathbound Is Still Awful in Madness. How Many Male Awakeners Have to Fail?

content:
2. His kit feels like several different ideas stitched together
Almost every major part of Gogier's kit tells you that Defense and Shield generation are supposed to be his core identity.
His Rouse increases the Base Shield provided by Defense.
His Absolute Axiom raises that bonus all the way to +100% Base Shield.
His signature Wheel of Destiny further increases the Base Shield generated by the equipped Awakener's Defense by 50%, while also granting STR.
Everything points toward one clear identity:
Defense → Shield → survive pressure → convert that defensive investment into value.
And then we get an Enlighten that makes his Strike take effect an additional time.
Why?
What exactly is that supposed to do for his core gameplay loop?
How does that meaningfully support the defensive identity the rest of his kit is built around?
It feels completely disconnected from the character.
And then there is his Over-Exaltation.
Its entire effect is basically to make the STR gained from his Exalt three times higher.
That's it.
No meaningful new interaction.
No major change to his gameplay loop.
No mechanic that fixes the problems his base kit already has.
Now compare that with Vortice.
Her Over-Exaltation does not simply give her a slightly bigger number. It improves her offensive scaling and also gives her additional activations tied directly to the way her kit is supposed to function.
That is what an Over-Exaltation should feel like:
better numbers and a meaningful mechanical upgrade.
Then look at Caraboo.
Her Over-Exaltation directly gives her access to additional Blessing value, something that is already central to how her kit works.
Again, the upgrade reinforces the character's actual gameplay identity instead of pulling her in a completely different direction.
Now come back to Gogier.
At my investment level, his Over-Exaltation gives me less than 300 additional STR in actual play.
Who is that supposed to impress?
For something locked behind such heavy investment, it feels unbelievably dry.
No interesting mechanical evolution.
No real solution to his weaknesses.

content:
6. Now let's compare the male and female characters
Male characters:
Gogier: Oathbound, Pontos, Doresain, Pickman, Pollux, Castor
Female characters:
Doll: Inferno, Kathigu-Ra, Mouchette, Lotan: Cetarchon, Vortice, Murphy: Fauxborn, Saya, Xu, Caraboo, Arachne, Clementine, Corposant
Just look at those two groups.
Among the male characters, Pontos, Pollux and Castor at least save some face.
But even they are hardly dominating the current environment.
The other half ranges from awkward and highly situational to severely underpowered in Madness.
Now look at the female side.
Sure, Mouchette and Lotan: Cetarchon feel somewhat more strained in Madness right now.
But most of the others are strong, flexible, mechanically coherent, useful across multiple teams, or some combination of all four.
Some of them are ridiculously good.
So I have to ask:
What exactly is the intended position of male Awakeners in this game?
Having fewer male characters is one thing.
That is a design choice, and players can decide whether they are okay with it.
But having fewer male characters while repeatedly giving them weaker numbers, clunkier mechanics, worse returns on investment and shorter competitive lifespans is a completely different problem.
At this point, it is becoming increasingly difficult to dismiss the pattern as coincidence.
Players have every reason to question whether there is a systematic design bias against male Awakeners.
Nobody is asking for every male character to be broken.
Nobody is asking for them to automatically be stronger than female characters.
We are asking why so many of them keep getting the short end of the stick.

This part should not be controversial.
Gogier costs the same premium currency.
Doresain cost the same premium currency.
Pickman cost the same premium currency.
Their Wheels of Destiny cost the same resources.
Their duplicates cost the same money.
So why is the difference in actual value allowed to become this enormous?
If weaker characters were clearly being designed as pieces of future team archetypes, then maybe players could at least understand the long-term direction.
But with characters like Doresain and Gogier, I don't even see that future.
I don't look at these characters and think:
“Okay, they are just waiting for the final piece of their team.”
I look at them and see kits whose basic numbers and internal mechanics already struggle to function in the content that exists right now.
That is a completely different issue.

content:
8. Too many limited characters are already falling out of Madness
At this point, my problem is bigger than Gogier.
Too many limited characters simply cannot keep up with the current Madness tuning.
This is especially obvious with characters from Astral Reign.
These characters are still part of the current story era, yet some of them have already fallen out of what players can reasonably call a healthy endgame roster.
That is absurd.
You previously said that clearing the new D-Effect Zone should not require Over-Exaltation or Absolute Axiom-level investment as the baseline for stage balance.
So look at the game now.
There are characters who can have Absolute Axiom and still struggle to clear comfortably.
In some cases, they only manage it because another overtuned support is doing most of the heavy lifting.
So what exactly is the expected lifespan of a limited character in Morimens?
If I can spend the full cost to obtain a limited Awakener, spend even more to reach Psyche Surge +12, max their Wheel of Destiny, unlock their highest-investment systems, and then watch that character struggle in endgame content while they are still part of the current story era...
What exactly am I supposed to expect when the next banner appears?
And when a brand-new +12/+12 limited Warden cannot reasonably deal with the endgame environment he was released into, at what point does this stop being a normal balance problem and start becoming a serious problem with the value players are being sold?
I am not asking every new character to powercreep the previous one.
I do not want endless powercreep.
I am asking for three extremely basic things:
Competent numbers.
Coherent design.
Reasonable value for the investment being demanded from players.
Right now, Gogier: Oathbound does not meet that standard.
And unfortunately, he is not the first male limited Awakener to make me ask this question.

First time posting on the discord in over a year but GOgier's kit feels so bad that i feel compelled. Why is his 2-cost so much worse than every other corrosion source in the game unless you have AA and stall for 20 turns? Castor's plumes - 0 cost, retain, give passive shield; Saya - 0 cost, retain, aoe scales with enemy hp;  Caraboo's exalt - aoe corrosion while giving more shield than GOgier's exalt. Why is his X-cost capped at 5 arithmetica and why is the str-down so undertuned? Both Pontos and base Ogier have uncapped X-costs. Why are the base stats on his exalt so undertuned? Agrippa's exalt gives more shield and str while also providing alert and poison. I get the intention to boost his exalt through undertow stacks but the payoff just isn't there when the base stats are so bad.

Some suggestions for possible buffs: Give his 2-cost retain and/or change it to a 1-cost or even 0-cost. Make his E2 actually count as playing two strikes for stuff like GLotan's long blade and Mouchette.  Buff the numbers on his X-cost and exalt.
